title: Product successor relation payload schema documents (13 relations)
description: The registered payload schema DOCUMENT for fact2 relation payloads, named by identity-and-evidence section 3 and native-evidence section 4.4. fact.payloadSchemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of the EXACT FULL BYTES of this file; validation uses the selector the payload registry row names, exactly as the native and workflow import registries already work. This document has no root type on purpose: it is a multi-record bundle, and a bundle is admitted through its registry row, never by validating a payload against the whole document. ENCODING SUCCESSOR: fact2 payloads are canonical JSON C, not the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile. Every logical restriction that profile carried survives here as an admission rule - NFC text, no negative integers, closed field sets, enums, per-rung required/forbidden fields and the universe rule. Historical FactRecord1 CBOR bytes and their provenance are unchanged and remain valid history; they are never a fact2 preimage.

x-opensip-relation-registry.standing: Normative. Closed at 13 relations: the twelve inherited from fact-plane.v1 relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1 plus native-evidence section 4.4 unresolved-edge.
x-opensip-relation-registry.payloadSchemaDigest: raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of that file

bodyIdentityJoin.levelSpecificationRetained: normalisationVersion names the retained level specification bytes
bodyIdentityJoin.note: At L0 the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes, so the host recomputes it from the enclosing fact anchor: a real source join. At L1-L3 it is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute, so the requirement is exact retained preimage custody plus the framed-identity check. This is custody and framing evidence; it qualifies no normalizer.
bodyIdentityJoin.anchorRule: A clones fact carries exactly one anchor: the body span the identity is over. Zero anchors would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice, which is the arbitrary-anchor defect in another form.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdSource: the language of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row
bodyIdentityJoin.languageVersionSource: the raw 32 bytes of SHA-256(C(body-language-version)), the closed DERIVED record at foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/body-language-version, rebuilt by Run closure from the universe ResolvedInputs and the admitted retained native context the universe own nativeContextId names, per that universe domain languageVersionBinding. It carries the identity of the component that INTERPRETS the body span plus the selected source dialect; it never carries a human display string, an option-synthesis version, an operational platform value, a path, or a whole per-crate map. Fixed width, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length.
bodyIdentityJoin.tokenStreamFraming: u32be token_count || token*, token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id || u32be value_len || value. The closure parses the retained L1-L3 stream to prove custody and framing; it does not and must not judge the tokenisation itself.

snapshotJoins.note: anchorPathField closes the second-owner case: a file payload is admissible only under a fact whose every anchor lies in the very file the payload claims, so an arbitrary anchor can never be borrowed to satisfy a foreign file claim.

unresolved-edge.owner: native-evidence section 4.4 (new registry entry; not in inherited fact-plane.v1)

x-opensip-relation-registry.snapshotJoinLaw: Normative. Each row states what the enclosing fact snapshot must contain for this relation payload to be admissible. Rows are applied by identity-model close_run on every owning fact; a relation absent from this table declares that it names no snapshot path and no retained artifact, which is itself the record that nothing constrains it.

CallsPayloadV1.description: Product successor of inherited opensip.relation.calls.v1 (fact-plane.v1 relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1). Field set, types, enums, required and optional members are reproduced exactly; only the canonical ENCODING is superseded (C, not CBOR).

CanonicalPath.description: Inherited CanonicalPath: non-empty NFC project-relative path, slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash or backslash.

CanonicalText.description: Inherited CanonicalText: non-empty NFC text with no C0/C1 control characters. NFC text is an ADMISSION rule, not an encoder rule: C never normalizes. The host admits a relation payload only when every text value is already NFC, exactly as the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile required, and refuses otherwise.

x-opensip-digest.codec: SHA-256 over the fully framed domain-separated preimage: u8 len||domainTag, u8 len||levelId, u8 len||levelVersion (RAW 32 bytes, not hexadecimal display text), u8 len||languageId, u8 len||languageVersion, u32be len||payload. Unframed concatenation is FORBIDDEN.

payloadEncoding.L0-verbatim: u32be raw_byte_len || exact snapshot body-span bytes; tokenisation forbidden

x-opensip-digest.join: the frame is retained under the 64-hex suffix, so SHA-256(retained frame) equals it; the closure parses the frame and requires domainTag, levelId == normalisationLevel, levelVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of normalisationVersion, languageId from the fact sourceUniverse domain row, languageVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of the recomputed body-language-version projection, and at L0-verbatim the payload equals the enclosing fact anchor span bytes
x-opensip-digest.neverEquals: FACT-ID-V1. The fact identity wraps the complete clone fact and can never equal or substitute for bodyIdentity, by type or by domain (docs/coop/artifacts/fact-identity-policy.v2.json#/factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1/clonePayloadJoin).

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact retained canonical LEVEL SPECIFICATION bytes for this normalisation level: per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order and replacement byte rules
x-opensip-digest.note: A human semantic-version label alone is insufficient, and this is never an opaque caller hash.

x-opensip-digest-law.standing: The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every DigestHex, Sha256Text and CanonicalPath field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, producing preimage, codec, retention and owning authority. There is no default and no residue: a new such field added without an annotation is inadmissible. Coverage is asserted by consumed CHECKS in the Run closure, not by counting annotations.

retention.preimage: the exact preimage bytes are retained under this digest and the closure re-hashes them
retention.snapshot-inventoried: the value names a path in the analysed snapshot inventory, joined there
retention.provider-output-retained: the canonical payload is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute; its exact framed preimage is retained so an independent replay can re-hash it
retention.not-joined: the value names a state outside the analysed snapshot and is deliberately joined to nothing; the reason is stated on the field and the closure records the exemption rather than leaving it as residue

x-opensip-digest-law.enforcement: identity-model close_run applies the per-relation snapshotJoins and bodyIdentity joins below to EVERY owning fact, after registered-selector validation and independently of the payload decode cache. A payload alone cannot decide snapshot truth, so the enclosing fact, the snapshot, the retained blobs and the bound native context are required owner context.
x-opensip-digest-law.residueRule: Consumed, not declared. Every x-opensip-digest field of a relation selector must be reachable from that relation registry entry snapshotJoins or bodyIdentityJoin, or must declare retention not-joined with its reason. An annotated field with no join, a join naming a field the selector does not have, and an unannotated digest/path field are each inadmissible.
